```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
library(qualitas)
```

## Start with the observation unit

A quality assessment compares a data snapshot with requirements for its intended use. A specification describes columns, types, keys, ranges and missing-value codes. Rules describe relationships that valid records must satisfy. `assess()` evaluates those requirements and returns findings, measures and dimension scores.

This vignette uses a small synthetic intake table. Each row represents one interview. Two records share an identifier, one age is outside its allowed range, and one district is missing.

```{r intake}
intake <- data.frame(
  interview_id = c("I01", "I02", "I02", "I04"),
  age = c(28L, 240L, 41L, 35L),
  district = c("North", "South", "South", NA_character_),
  consent = c("yes", "yes", "yes", "yes")
)
intake
```

## Describe the requirements

`infer_spec()` provides a starting specification from the observed data. Review it against the questionnaire, data dictionary and analysis requirements. Inferred ranges and categories describe what is present; explicit requirements define what is valid.

Here, identifiers are required and unique, ages must be between 18 and 100, and district values must belong to the stated list. `spec_complete()` supplies the remaining specification fields.

```{r specification}
spec <- spec_complete(tibble::tibble(
  column = c("interview_id", "age", "district", "consent"),
  type = c("text", "integer", "category", "category"),
  role = c("id", "age", "group", ""),
  required = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE),
  unique = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),
  min = c(NA_character_, "18", NA_character_, NA_character_),
  max = c(NA_character_, "100", NA_character_, NA_character_),
  allowed = c(NA_character_, NA_character_, "North;South", "yes;no"),
  description = c("Interview identifier", "Age in completed years",
                  "District of interview", "Consent given")
))
result <- assess(intake, spec = spec, checks = c("CO02", "UN02", "VA02"),
                 name = "synthetic intake")
```

The selected checks evaluate required values, repeated keys and numeric ranges. Omit `checks` to run the full catalogue. Some checks need a declared column role or an optional package; inspect each measure's status to see what was evaluated.

## Read findings before the overall score

```{r findings}
issues(result)
measures(result)
scores(result)
```

`issues()` identifies the check, column, row and observed value behind each finding. Row coordinates refer to the assessed snapshot. A record may produce findings under more than one check, so the number of issues is not a count of distinct defective records.

Each check's measure identifies its observation unit and denominator. Its score is the share of assessed units that passed, calculated as `1 - flagged / checked` when a denominator is available. Dimension scores combine check scores using severity weights. Review the denominators, individual findings and assessment status alongside any summary score.

Statistical diagnostics such as age heaping, digit preference and interviewer differences identify patterns for investigation. Interpretation depends on the measurement process and population; a flag alone does not establish fabrication.

## Add a record-level rule

Rules are expressions that evaluate to `TRUE` for a valid record. This rule requires consent. Use reviewed rule expressions from a trusted source because they are evaluated as R expressions against the data.

```{r rules}
rule_result <- assess(intake, spec = spec, rules = c(consented = "consent == 'yes'"),
                      checks = "CS01", name = "synthetic consent review")
issues(rule_result)
```

## Record a correction and reassess

A cleaning log records the proposed action, replacement value, reason and decision maker. In this synthetic example, the exercise supplies a verified age of 24 for the second record. The duplicate identifier and missing district still require separate review.

```{r cleaning}
log <- cleaning_log(result)
log$action <- "keep"
log$reason <- "Retained pending review in this example"
selected <- which(log$column == "age" & log$row == 2L)
log$action[selected] <- "change"
log$new_value[selected] <- "24"
log$reason[selected] <- "The synthetic exercise specifies age 24"
log$decided_by[selected] <- "Example reviewer"
corrected <- apply_log(intake, log)
rechecked <- assess(corrected, spec = spec, checks = c("CO02", "UN02", "VA02"),
                    name = "reviewed synthetic intake")
issues(rechecked)
stopifnot(corrected$age[2] == 24L)
```

Reassessment shows which findings remain after the recorded decision. Retain the original snapshot and the applied log in the project's established data-management system.

## Compare deliveries

`compare_data()` describes changes between two deliveries, including column structure and distributions. Compare snapshots that represent the same observation unit and comparable populations.

```{r comparison}
comparison <- compare_data(intake, corrected)
comparison
```

## Export a report

`report()` writes HTML, or a Word document when its optional dependencies are installed. Reports include findings and observed values, so review them for confidential content before sharing. `max_issues` limits displayed findings while the assessment retains the complete findings table.

```{r report}
local({
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
  on.exit(unlink(path), add = TRUE)
  report(rechecked, path, max_issues = 20)
  stopifnot(file.exists(path), file.info(path)$size > 0)
})
```

Use a permanent output path when retaining a report. `write_results()` exports assessment tables and JSON; the installed function help describes its files and return value.

## Explore the larger synthetic survey

The package includes a synthetic survey with planted defects, together with its specification and rules. Its generator is maintained in the tests. Identifiers, telephone-like strings and free-text examples are generated fixtures, not collected respondent records.

```{r bundled-survey}
example_path <- system.file("extdata", "messy_survey.csv", package = "qualitas")
survey <- read.csv(example_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dim(survey)
checks_catalogue()[, c("check_id", "dimension")]
```

## Check a shared exchange contract

The contract helpers accept explicit requirements. They return defect tables without changing source records. Dictionary and indicator checks assess supplied declarations; the receiving team still checks coverage against the delivered fields and reviews their meaning.

```{r shared-contract}
dictionary <- data.frame(
  element_id = "site.identifier", table = "visits", column = "site_id",
  definition = "Persistent identifier of a physical site", type = "text",
  unit = "not applicable", owner = "Example IA", version = "1.0")
stopifnot(nrow(validate_dictionary(dictionary)) == 0L)
sites <- data.frame(ia = c("a", "b"), site_id = c("01", "01"))
visits <- data.frame(ia = c("a", "c"), site_id = c("01", "01"))
relation <- data.frame(from = "visits", table = "sites")
relation$columns <- relation$keys <- list(c("ia", "site_id"))
key_findings <- assess_keys(list(sites = sites, visits = visits),
  keys = list(sites = c("ia", "site_id")), relations = relation)
stopifnot(identical(key_findings$requirement, "foreign_unmatched"))
key_findings
```

Expected answers use a logical applicability mask supplied from the reviewed questionnaire. An unknown mask produces a review issue. Choice rules use declared codes and a literal separator; codes containing that separator need a child table.

```{r expected-answers}
answers <- data.frame(consent = c("yes", "no", NA), response = c("a;b", "a", NA))
assess_answers(answers, "response", answers$consent == "yes")
assess_choices(answers, "response", allowed = c("a", "b", "none"),
  multiple = TRUE, exclusive = "none")
counts <- data.frame(indicator_id = "visits", period = "2026-Q3", reported = 10, observed = 9)
stopifnot(reconcile_counts(counts)$status == "issues found")
```

`assess_delivery()` verifies relative file paths, SHA-256, declared file sizes when supplied, required document roles and timestamp forms. A manifest declaration cannot establish the sender's identity or whether a questionnaire is substantively adequate. `review_findings()` records decisions against the source hash, dataset locator and assessment contract, preserving machine flags and scores. Encryption, questionnaire interpretation, independent back-checks and restoration tests require evidence outside these functions.

## Reconcile revisions and compare groups

Record reconciliation requires complete, unique keys and matching column types. The results separate additions, removals and cell changes. A normalization function is explicit and can itself expose duplicate keys.

```{r record-revisions}
before <- data.frame(agency = c("a", "b"), id = c("01", "01"), count = c(4L, 6L))
after <- before
after$count[2] <- 7L
revision <- compare_records(before, after, keys = c("agency", "id"))
stopifnot(revision$matched == 2L, nrow(revision$changes) == 1L,
          revision$changes$column == "count")
revision$changes
```

A functional dependency tests whether one entity has consistent declared attributes. Distribution comparisons retain both group and reference denominators and leave sparse comparisons unassessed.

```{r grouped-comparisons}
places <- data.frame(site = c("s1", "s1", "s2"), district = c("d1", "d2", "d2"))
stopifnot(any(assess_dependencies(places, "site", "district")$results$flagged, na.rm = TRUE))
responses <- data.frame(enumerator = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 4),
                        answer = c(rep("yes", 4), rep("no", 4)))
shares <- assess_distributions(responses, "enumerator", "answer", min_n = 4,
                                difference = 0.3)
stopifnot(all(shares$results$flagged))
```

## Screen declared geographic evidence

Coordinates require an explicit WGS84 and longitude/latitude contract. Country or administrative containment requires a supplied polygon and its source version; a rectangle does not substitute for the polygon. Distances and clusters are screening signals requiring review.

```{r geographic-evidence}
visits <- data.frame(lon = c(0, 0, 200), lat = c(0, 0, 0),
  site = c("s1", "s1", "s2"), day = as.Date(rep("2026-11-25", 3)))
geo <- assess_geography(visits, "lon", "lat", crs = 4326,
  axis = "longitude_latitude", site = "site", day = "day", cluster_n = 2)
stopifnot(geo$results$pair[3] == "invalid", all(geo$results$clustered[1:2]))
```

`inspect_workbook()` returns saved XML facts, storage information and findings without source cell values. It does not authenticate an author or an encryption control. The package tests construct synthetic workbooks with planted structural faults, invalid relationships and untrusted XML, and compare the results with their declared fixtures.

`assess_questionnaire()` checks a structured instrument definition. `assess_requirements()` uses exact requirement and scope identities, evidence-file hashes and review metadata. They preserve the need for human interpretation, documented collection authority and actual operational trials.

## Method references

The check catalogue records the source and framework mapping for each check. The package draws on the harmonised terminology of Kahn et al. (2016), <https://doi.org/10.13063/2327-9214.1244>, the data-quality framework of Schmidt et al. (2021), <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12874-021-01252-7>, and the measurement approach of Pipino, Lee and Wang (2002), <https://doi.org/10.1145/505248.506010>. These mappings explain the package's organisation and do not represent formal certification against a standard.
